equivalents.note: The Tibetan has bdag ni shin tu rmongs, 'I was utterly deluded', where shin tu, 'utterly', stands in place of the sva- ('own') of svamohe, as if the translators read su-.
The Tibetan line reads bājule as a name, Rāhula (rA hu la yis, 'Rāhula gave me the mark'), while Munidatta's Sanskrit and its Tibetan gloss take the word as vajrakula, rdo rje'i rigs (cp.35.m5).
The line reads abhāge as cha shas med pa, 'partless, without share', which the Tibetan comment explains as the share of non-arising (ma skyes pa'i cha, cp.35.m6).
For vajraprabhāva, 'the power of the vajra', the Tibetan has rdo rje bla ma'i mthu, 'the power of the vajra guru'.
Here the Tibetan translates the name, bzang po'i zhabs, 'Excellent Foot', where the heading, m1 and the signature line transliterate it (b+ha dra).
Here ātmasvarūpa is rang gi ngo bo nyid, 'its own essence', not rang bzhin as in m2 and m4.

questions: citta at cp.35.m4: for ataeva cittasyānudayena, 'hence through the non-arising of mind', the Tibetan has de'i phyir bzhi pa shar bas, 'hence through the dawning of the fourth', with no word for mind; it seems to read something like caturthasyodayena. No equivalent is given.
